question: A leader who takes the group into confidence and takes decisions with their participation follows:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. democratic leadership

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A democratic leader consults the group, shares the decision and keeps the members informed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — autocratic leadership: An autocratic leader decides alone and issues orders

B — bureaucratic leadership: A bureaucratic leader goes simply by the rules

C — laissez faire leadership: A laissez faire leader leaves the group to itself

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nursing officer who discusses the duty roster with the staff gets a roster that is respected, because a decision that the staff have helped to make is the one they keep to

question: In an emergency such as a cardiac arrest, the leadership style that works best is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. autocratic, with clear and quick orders

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In an emergency there is no time to debate, so clear firm orders and one person in charge save the patient

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — democratic discussion before every step: Discussion before every step is impossible in an arrest

C — a vote among the team members: Voting has no place in an emergency

D — laissez faire: A loosely led team in an arrest wastes the minutes that decide the outcome

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse in charge assigns tasks by name during an arrest, because a call to the whole group leaves each person waiting for someone else to move

question: A newly posted nursing officer with 15 junior nurses gives each nurse complete freedom to plan her own work. Within a week the ward work is disorganised. This style is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. laissez faire and unsuitable for a new group

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A laissez faire leader gives the group full freedom, which fails when the group is new and needs direction

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — democratic: A democratic leader still guides the group and takes part in the decisions

B — transformational: A transformational leader inspires the group towards a shared goal and does not simply stand aside

D — autocratic: An autocratic leader gives orders rather than freedom

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse gives more freedom as the group becomes confident, because freedom given to a group that has not yet learnt the work is not delegation but neglect
option_3: laissez faire and unsuitable for a new group

question: A leader who changes her style according to the situation and the readiness of the group follows:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. situational leadership

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A situational leader judges the situation and the readiness of the group and leads firmly or freely as the case needs

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — trait leadership: Trait theory holds that leaders are born with certain qualities

B — laissez faire leadership: A laissez faire leader leaves the group alone in every situation

D — bureaucratic leadership: A bureaucratic leader goes by the rules in every situation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse leads firmly when an emergency is on and consults when a routine change is planned, because one style for every situation is the mark of a leader who is not watching the ward

question: Two staff nurses quarrel over who should escort a patient to the X-ray room. The nursing officer's best step is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. bring both together, hear the reason for the quarrel and settle the duty so that both accept it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Hearing both sides of a small conflict and settling the duty fairly removes the cause and keeps the group working

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — report both of them for indiscipline: A report for such a small matter hardens both the nurses

B — order one of them to go and close the matter: An order settles the task for the hour and leaves the ill feeling behind

D — shift both to another ward: Shifting both only moves the conflict to another ward

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse listens to each person separately first and then together, because a person who has been allowed to state her own case is far less likely to go on arguing
option_2: order one of them to go and close the matter
option_3: bring both together, hear the reason for the quarrel and settle the duty so that both accept it

question: A common cause of conflict among the nursing staff in a ward is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. an unclear division of duties and responsibilities

🧠 Clinical Rationale: When duties overlap or are not clear, two nurses either both do a task or both leave it, and the quarrel follows

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a written nursing procedure: A written procedure removes doubt about the method

C — a regular ward meeting: A ward meeting gives a place to settle differences

D — a well displayed duty roster: A clearly displayed roster reduces conflict

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse in charge writes who is responsible for what at the start of every shift, because most quarrels in a ward are about a task that each nurse believed belonged to the other
option_2: an unclear division of duties and responsibilities

question: A staff nurse complains in writing that she has been given night duty every time though her turn has come for the morning shift. The nursing officer should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. look into the roster, correct the unfairness and reply to her in writing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A written grievance is examined, set right if it is genuine and answered in writing so that the nurse knows her complaint was heard

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ignore the complaint as trivial: Ignoring a complaint is what turns it into a lasting quarrel

C — reduce her leave: Any punishment for making a complaint is unfair and wrong

D — tell her to accept what she is given: A refusal without a reason drives the matter further

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse replies within a fixed time and keeps a copy, because a grievance that is left unanswered for weeks is one that is later raised outside the ward
option_2: look into the roster, correct the unfairness and reply to her in writing
option_4: tell her to accept what she is given

question: Downward communication in a hospital means the flow of information:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. from the seniors to the junior staff

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Downward communication passes from the higher level to the lower, such as an order or a policy from the office to the ward

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — among nurses of the same grade only: Communication among equals is horizontal

C — outside the hospital: Communication with the public is external

D — from the junior staff to the seniors: Communication from the junior to the senior is upward

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse in charge passes an important order on in the same words and later checks that it was understood, because an order that is passed along the line in different words at each level arrives changed
option_1: from the seniors to the junior staff
option_2: among nurses of the same grade only
option_4: from the junior staff to the seniors

question: A nursing officer wishes to reduce the staff turnover in her ward. The step most likely to help is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. recognise good work, give a hearing to the difficulties and plan the duties fairly

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Staff stay where their work is recognised, their difficulties are heard and the duty is fair

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — increase the number of inspections: More inspections increase the pressure without improving the satisfaction

B — stop holding ward meetings: Stopping the meetings removes the one place where difficulties are raised

C — threaten the staff with transfer: A threat makes the staff leave sooner

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse names the person and the specific work when she thanks the staff, because general praise is pleasant to hear and specific recognition is the one that is remembered
option_4: recognise good work, give a hearing to the difficulties and plan the duties fairly

question: A nursing officer has to start a new documentation system in a ward of 20 nurses who are used to the old one. Her best step is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. explain the reason for the change, invite a few nurses to try it first and then introduce it for the whole ward

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A change is accepted when the reason is explained and a few staff try it first and report, which is the unfreezing step of a planned change

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — put up the new forms without any explanation: A change put up without explanation is quietly worked around

C — warn the staff of disciplinary action for any delay: A warning creates resentment and hidden resistance

D — introduce it only when an inspection is due: A change kept for an inspection teaches the staff that it is not meant for real work

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse listens to the difficulties found in the trial and alters the form if needed, because a system that is modified from the remarks of the users is the one that survives
option_1: explain the reason for the change, invite a few nurses to try it first and then introduce it for the whole ward
option_2: put up the new forms without any explanation
option_3: warn the staff of disciplinary action for any delay
option_4: introduce it only when an inspection is due

question: The confidential report of a nurse is written mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. record her work, conduct and potential for the use of promotion and posting

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The report records the work, the conduct and the promise of the person and is used for promotion, posting and training

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — compare her with her friends: Comparison with colleagues is not its aim, though performance is judged against the standard

B — fill the office file: It is not a formality for the file

D — punish her for past faults: It is not a means of punishment

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse shows the report to the person and takes her signature, because a remark that the person has never been told about cannot help her improve
option_3: record her work, conduct and potential for the use of promotion and posting

question: A nurse reports for duty smelling of alcohol and is unsteady on her feet. The nurse in charge should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. remove her from patient care at once, arrange for another nurse to cover the shift and report the matter to the higher authority

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A nurse who is not fit to work is removed from patient care at once, the shift is covered and the incident is reported so that the person gets help as well as the ward being protected

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — allow her to work but watch her: Watching her still leaves the patients at risk

B — make her drink strong coffee and start work: Coffee does not make her fit for duty

C — send her home quietly and say nothing: Sending her home quietly hides the problem and leaves her without help

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the observation plainly and follows the staff welfare policy, because the aim is both to protect the patients and to give the nurse the treatment she needs
option_1: allow her to work but watch her
option_2: make her drink strong coffee and start work
option_3: send her home quietly and say nothing
option_4: remove her from patient care at once, arrange for another nurse to cover the shift and report the matter to the higher authority

question: The first step in solving a ward problem in an orderly way is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. define the problem clearly and collect the facts about it

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A problem is first stated clearly and the facts about it are gathered, for a decision taken before the problem is understood only shifts it about

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — report it to the office: Reporting without facts gives the office nothing to act on

C — call a meeting of the whole staff: A meeting called before the facts are known produces opinions and not a solution

D — choose a remedy at once: A remedy chosen before the problem is understood treats the wrong thing

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the problem in one sentence that anyone can read, because a problem that cannot be stated simply has not been understood yet
option_1: define the problem clearly and collect the facts about it
option_3: call a meeting of the whole staff

question: A research design is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the plan that shows how the study will be carried out to answer the question

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The design sets out the approach, the setting, the sample and the way the data will be collected and analysed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the final report of the study: The report comes at the end

B — the list of the references: References belong to the report

D — the name of the researcher: The name of the researcher is not a design

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the design before beginning the study, because a study that sets out without a design collects data that cannot answer its own question
option_3: the plan that shows how the study will be carried out to answer the question

question: A study that counts how many nurses in a hospital have received the influenza vaccine is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. quantitative research

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Quantitative research measures and counts numbers, as in this count of the nurses vaccinated

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a clinical trial: A clinical trial tests a treatment

C — an experimental study: An experimental study introduces a change and compares the effect

D — qualitative research: Qualitative research explores feelings, experiences and meanings in words

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse chooses the approach from the question and not from the fashion, because a question that asks how many needs numbers while a question that asks how it felt needs words

question: In a true experimental study the participants are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. allotted to the groups at random

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Random allotment of the participants to the treatment and the control group is the mark of a true experiment and keeps the two groups alike

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — told which group they are in: Telling the participants which group they are in destroys blinding and can alter the result

B — always nurses: The participants are the persons the question concerns and not always nurses

D — chosen by the researcher as he likes: Allotment by the researcher's choice allows bias

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks that the two groups were alike to begin with, because a difference that was already there before the treatment is not a result of the treatment
option_4: chosen by the researcher as he likes

question: A design in which the groups are already made, as when one ward is compared with another, is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a quasi experimental design

🧠 Clinical Rationale: When the groups already exist and cannot be allotted at random, the study is quasi experimental

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a true experiment: A true experiment needs random allotment

B — a case report: A case report describes one patient

D — a pilot study: A pilot study is a small trial run of the tool

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse states clearly that the groups were not randomised, because a reader who is not told this may take a finding from two wards as proof of a treatment

question: A researcher studies whether the hours of sleep of 50 nurses are related to the number of errors they make. This study is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. correlational

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The study looks for a relation between two things as they already exist, which is a correlational design

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a case study: A case study describes one person in depth

C — experimental: Nothing is changed by the researcher, so it is not experimental

D — a clinical trial: A clinical trial tests a treatment

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse remembers that a relation is not a cause, because two things that move together may both be moved by a third factor that no one has measured

question: Before using a new questionnaire the researcher gets it examined by a panel of experts in order to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. establish its content validity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A panel of experts judges whether the questions cover the whole subject they are meant to measure, which is content validity

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — establish its price: The price of the tool is not the purpose

B — shorten it: Shortening is a different matter

C — find the sample size: The sample size is worked out by a separate calculation

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse gives the panel a copy of the objectives along with the tool, because a panel that judges the questions without seeing the aim cannot say whether anything has been left out

question: A researcher has a complete list of all the 400 nurses of a hospital and wants to draw 80 of them. The list used for the drawing is called the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. sampling frame

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The sampling frame is the full list from which the sample is drawn, and here it is the list of the 400 nurses

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — sample: The sample is the 80 who are actually chosen

B — target population: The target population is the whole group about which the conclusion is drawn

C — control group: The control group belongs to the design of an experiment

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks the frame for names entered twice or missing altogether, because a frame with names left out gives every one of those persons no chance of being chosen

question: The researcher picks five whole wards out of twenty and studies every nurse in those wards. This is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. cluster sampling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Whole groups, here the wards, are chosen and all the members within them are studied, which is cluster sampling

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — quota sampling: Quota sampling fills a fixed number in each group

B — simple random sampling: Simple random sampling draws individuals from a single list

C — purposive sampling: Purposive sampling chooses the members the researcher judges suitable

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes that in cluster sampling the persons within a ward are alike, so the true sample is the number of clusters and not the number of nurses, which affects the analysis

question: A study reports that in a sample of 30 nurses the mean hand washing score was higher in the trained group by 0.5, with a p value of 0.40. The nurse should conclude that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the small difference is not significant and the study was too small to show a real effect

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A p value of 0.40 is well above the accepted level, so the small difference could easily have come about by chance and a study of this size cannot settle the question

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the result proves that training is unnecessary: A result that is not significant does not prove that training is useless, only that this study did not show a benefit

B — training makes hand washing worse: Nothing in the result suggests harm

D — the training has clearly improved hand washing: A difference with such a p value is not proof of an effect

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the number in the sample along with the result, because a small study that finds no significant difference is the call for a larger study and not for a change of practice
option_1: the result proves that training is unnecessary
option_3: the small difference is not significant and the study was too small to show a real effect
option_4: the training has clearly improved hand washing

question: A researcher finds that the mean income of the patients is far higher than the income of most of them. The measure that describes the group better here is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. median

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A few very high values pull the mean upward, while the median, being the middle value, is not disturbed by them and describes the group better

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — total: The total tells nothing about a typical value

C — range: The range only gives the gap between the highest and the lowest

D — mean: The mean is exactly the measure that is distorted here

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reports the median for a skewed figure such as income or length of stay, because one patient who stayed for months can make the mean describe a ward that does not exist

question: A researcher gives the same questionnaire to the same group twice, a fortnight apart, and compares the two sets of answers. She is testing the tool's:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. test retest reliability

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Giving the same tool twice to the same people and finding the answers alike shows that the tool gives a steady result, which is test retest reliability

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — content validity: Content validity is judged by experts and not by repeating the tool

C — length: The length of the tool is a separate matter

D — cost: The cost of the tool is not measured this way

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps the interval long enough for the memory of the answers to fade and short enough for the condition to be unchanged, because an interval that is too short tests the memory rather than the tool

question: A tool that measures what it is meant to measure, and no more and no less, is said to have:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. validity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Validity is the degree to which an instrument measures the exact quality it claims to measure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — objectivity: Objectivity is freedom from personal bias

B — practicability: Practicability is the ease of use

D — reliability: Reliability is the steadiness of the measurement, which is a different quality

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks the validity before using a scale, because a tool that reliably measures the wrong thing gives a whole set of figures that are precise and useless at the same time

question: In the report of a research study the discussion section is meant to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. interpret the findings, compare them with earlier work and state the limitations

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The discussion explains what the findings mean, compares them with other studies and states honestly what the study could not settle

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — describe the hospital in which it was done: A description of the setting belongs to the methods

C — list the names of the authors: The names of the authors come on the title page

D — repeat the whole list of the raw data: The raw data belong in the tables and not in the discussion

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reads the limitations before acting on a study, because every study has some and a report that admits none has not been written honestly
option_1: interpret the findings, compare them with earlier work and state the limitations
option_2: describe the hospital in which it was done
option_4: repeat the whole list of the raw data

question: According to the code of professional conduct, the first duty of a nurse is towards:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the patient

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The care and the safety of the patient come before every other interest in nursing practice

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the medical officer: The doctor's orders are carried out within the limits of safety and not without question

C — the nursing council: The council regulates the profession and is not the first duty

D — the hospital management: The management has a claim on the nurse's service but not before the patient

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who keeps the patient first in every decision finds that the other duties fall into their proper place, because a nurse who serves the patient honestly serves the institution too

question: The right of a patient to refuse a treatment is based on the principle of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. respect for the autonomy of the person

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Respect for autonomy means that a person of sound mind may accept or refuse what is offered, even when the refusal is against medical advice

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — justice: Justice is fairness in the distribution of care

B — confidentiality: Confidentiality is the duty to keep the patient's information private

D — beneficence: Beneficence is doing good for the patient and does not overrule a clear refusal

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records a refusal in the patient's own words and reports it to the doctor, because a refusal that has been clearly written down protects the patient's right and the nurse's integrity alike
option_3: respect for the autonomy of the person

question: During an enquiry into a death in the ward the nurse's record is the chief document. This is because a record:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. made at the time of the event is evidence of what was actually observed and done

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A record written at the time by the nurse who was there is the best evidence of the facts, and it is admitted as such

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — is written in the nurse's own language: A record is written in plain professional language without any comment about others

C — is kept only for the family: The record serves the patient, the team and the enquiry, and not the family alone

D — can be written any time before the enquiry: A record written after the enquiry has begun loses its value at once

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes what was seen and done and never an opinion about a colleague, because a note that blames another person weakens the whole record and starts a quarrel inside the team
option_1: made at the time of the event is evidence of what was actually observed and done
option_2: is written in the nurse's own language
option_4: can be written any time before the enquiry

question: A nurse who works in a private clinic while on sick leave from the hospital is guilty of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. professional misconduct

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Claiming to be unfit while working elsewhere is a breach of the conditions of service and of professional conduct

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a criminal offence: It is a matter of discipline and not of criminal law

C — a lapse of etiquette only: It goes beyond a matter of manners

D — nothing at all: It is plainly a fault

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who is genuinely ill rests completely and sends the fitness certificate on time, because a sick leave that is misused damages the trust that the whole staff depends on

question: In a case of a patient declared brain dead, the removal of an organ for donation requires:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. consent given as per the law, such as the patient's pledge or the family's consent certified by the prescribed authority

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The law lays down the way consent is given and certified, whether by the patient's own pledge or by the family with the approval of the competent authority

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the consent of the nurse in charge: A nurse may not give consent for such a step and is only a part of the team

B — the consent of the ward boy: A ward employee has no role in consent

C — no consent at all: Consent is the heart of the whole matter

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse knows the hospital's protocol and calls the transplant coordinator at the right time, because a step taken outside the protocol makes the whole donation unlawful and must be undone
option_1: the consent of the nurse in charge
option_4: consent given as per the law, such as the patient's pledge or the family's consent certified by the prescribed authority

question: When a patient with a terminal illness wishes to stop further curative treatment, the nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. respect the patient's informed decision and help to arrange care that keeps him comfortable

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A patient of sound mind may decline treatment, and the nurse then helps to arrange palliative care that eases the pain and keeps the dignity of the patient

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — hide the diagnosis from the family: A family is kept informed with the patient's consent

C — sign the order to stop treatment herself: A nurse does not write an order or give consent for the patient

D — persuade the patient to continue at any cost: Persuading against the patient's own wish takes away his right over himself

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse listens to what the patient actually wants and does not assume that the family, however loving, speaks for him
option_1: respect the patient's informed decision and help to arrange care that keeps him comfortable
option_3: sign the order to stop treatment herself
option_4: persuade the patient to continue at any cost

question: A sudden change in the structure of a gene is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a mutation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A mutation is a change in the sequence of the gene, and it may be passed on to the children

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a karyotype: A karyotype is a picture of the chromosomes

B — a pedigree: A pedigree is a chart of the family

C — a phenotype: A phenotype is the outward appearance that results from the genes

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains that most mutations do no harm and only an occasional one causes disease, because a family that has heard the word mutation often fears that every illness in the house is inherited

question: An example of a disease inherited as an autosomal dominant trait is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. achondroplasia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Achondroplasia, a form of short limbed dwarfism, is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait and appears in every generation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — thalassaemia: Thalassaemia is also autosomal recessive

C — sickle cell anaemia: Sickle cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive trait

D — cystic fibrosis: Cystic fibrosis is autosomal recessive

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains that in a dominant trait an affected person has an affected parent and each child has one chance in two, because this is the pattern a family can be shown and understood

question: A disorder caused by an abnormality in the number of chromosomes differs from a gene disorder in that it:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. affects many systems of the body and is usually detected by karyotyping

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A change in the number of chromosomes affects many parts of the body at once and is seen on a karyotype, unlike a fault in a single gene

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — affects only the skin: The effect is on the whole body and not on the skin alone

B — is caused by an infection: An infection does not change the number of chromosomes

D — is always mild: Such disorders are often serious and not mild

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse watches for more than one problem in the same child, because a baby with feeding difficulty, a heart murmur and unusual features may have one chromosomal cause behind all of them
option_3: affects many systems of the body and is usually detected by karyotyping

question: A genetic screening programme in a community is carried out mainly to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. find the persons with a genetic risk early so that they can be counselled and treated

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Screening finds the persons at risk early, so that counselling, early treatment and prevention are possible

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — satisfy the health authority only: The satisfaction of the authority is not the purpose of a screening programme

C — reduce the population: Reducing the population is not its aim

D — separate the affected persons from society: Screening is never a means of separation, which would be unjust and harmful

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains to the community what the screening can and cannot do before it begins, because a test whose meaning is not understood becomes the source of fear and refusal
option_2: find the persons with a genetic risk early so that they can be counselled and treated

question: Which of the following is used to examine the chromosomes of a fetus before birth?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. karyotyping of the cells obtained by amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cells containing the chromosomes of the fetus are obtained by amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling and are then cultured for a karyotype

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a simple blood test of the mother: A blood test of the mother does not show the chromosomes of the fetus

C — an abdominal X-ray: An X-ray shows the bones and not the chromosomes

D — the mother's weight record: The weight record has nothing to do with the chromosomes

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse tells the parents that the report takes some weeks because the cells must grow first, since a family left without that information fills the waiting time with worst fears
option_1: a simple blood test of the mother
option_2: karyotyping of the cells obtained by amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling

question: A nurse handling the results of a genetic test must:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. keep the result confidential and share it only with the person tested and those he names

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A genetic result belongs to the person tested, and it is shared only with him and with those he chooses; other relatives are told only with his consent after counselling

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — record it on the front of the case sheet: A note on the cover exposes the result to everyone who handles the file

C — inform the employer of the person: The employer has no right to it

D — tell the whole family at once: Informing the whole family against his wish breaches his confidentiality

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse talks to the person alone first and then helps him decide how to tell the relatives who may also be at risk, because a result that leaks without consent destroys the trust the whole programme rests on
option_1: record it on the front of the case sheet
option_2: keep the result confidential and share it only with the person tested and those he names

question: The first thing the nurse does when a new patient is admitted to the ward is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. receive the patient, identify him and make him comfortable in bed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The nurse receives the patient, confirms his identity from the papers and settles him in bed before anything else

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — send him to the X-ray room at once: Investigations are arranged after the admission assessment

C — ask for the payment of the bill: The bill is not the nurse's work

D — give the evening drugs: Drugs are given after the patient has been received and assessed

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse introduces herself and shows the patient the call bell first, because a patient who knows who is looking after him and how to call for help settles far sooner
option_1: send him to the X-ray room at once
option_2: receive the patient, identify him and make him comfortable in bed
option_3: ask for the payment of the bill

question: A 75-year-old man admitted with giddiness tries to get up to the toilet without help. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. keep the bed low with the side rails up, keep the call bell within reach and help him to the toilet himself

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A low bed, the side rails raised, the call bell at hand and the nurse helping him to the toilet removes the reason for the fall

🔍 Key Clues: 75-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — restrain him to the bed: Restraint is used only when nothing else will prevent injury and would frighten him

B — shift him to a bed near the window: A bed by the window does not reduce the risk

D — tell him not to move at all: An order not to move is forgotten in minutes

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse asks an elderly patient to walk a few steps with support on admission, because the way he walks tells her how much help he needs and where a fall will happen
option_2: shift him to a bed near the window
option_3: keep the bed low with the side rails up, keep the call bell within reach and help him to the toilet himself
option_4: tell him not to move at all

question: The nurse must wash her hands after removing the gloves because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a small hole in the glove or a slip while removing it leaves the hands contaminated

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Gloves may have a tiny tear, and they can be contaminated while being taken off, so the hands are washed afterwards

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the gloves are costly: Cost has nothing to do with the practice

B — the soap is free of cost: Free soap is not the reason

C — the gloves make the hands sweat: Sweating is not the reason

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse removes the gloves without touching the outer surface with the bare hand, because a glove pulled off carelessly leaves the very organisms it was worn to keep away
option_4: a small hole in the glove or a slip while removing it leaves the hands contaminated

question: A nurse notices a mistake in her own earlier entry in the chart. The correct way to correct it is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. draw a single line through it, write the correction, sign and date it, and leave the original readable

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The wrong entry is struck through with a single line so that it can still be read, and the correction is written, signed and dated beside it

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — erase the entry and write it again: Erasing or using correction fluid makes the record look altered and destroys its value

B — tear out the page: Tearing out a page throws away the whole record

C — write over the mistake with the pen: Writing over the words makes both entries unreadable

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the reason for the correction as a word or two beside it, because a change that carries no explanation is the first thing an enquiry looks at
option_1: erase the entry and write it again
option_3: write over the mistake with the pen
option_4: draw a single line through it, write the correction, sign and date it, and leave the original readable

question: A 30-year-old man on the third day after a fever has a temperature of 36.4 degrees Celsius and feels well. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. record it as a normal reading and continue the routine care

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A temperature of 36.4 degrees Celsius is within the normal range, so the reading is recorded and the routine care continues

🔍 Key Clues: 30-year-old | 36.4 degrees Celsius

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — withhold the next meal: Withholding food is not required

B — give a hot water bottle and cover him with blankets: Extra warmth is unnecessary and causes discomfort

D — report a low temperature as an emergency: A normal reading is not an emergency

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse compares each reading with the earlier ones on the chart, because a fall to the normal range after a fever is a good sign and not a reportable event
option_2: give a hot water bottle and cover him with blankets
option_3: record it as a normal reading and continue the routine care
option_4: report a low temperature as an emergency

question: A patient with diabetes is sweating, trembling and confused and his blood sugar is 44 mg/dL. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. give a fast acting sugar by mouth if he can swallow, and check the sugar again after fifteen minutes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: These are the signs of hypoglycaemia, and a fast acting sugar given at once corrects the level quickly if the patient can swallow

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — withhold all food and drink: Withholding food in hypoglycaemia is dangerous

C — give a high protein meal: A protein meal acts too slowly to correct a low sugar

D — give his next insulin dose: Insulin would lower the sugar further

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse stays with the patient and repeats the sugar reading after fifteen minutes, because a single dose of sugar may not be enough to hold the level up until the next meal
option_2: give a fast acting sugar by mouth if he can swallow, and check the sugar again after fifteen minutes

question: To clear the air passages in a patient who can cough, the nurse should encourage:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. deep breathing and coughing with the wound or the chest supported

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Deep breathing and an effective cough clear the secretions, and supporting the chest or the wound reduces the pain and makes the cough work

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the use of a tight abdominal binder: A tight binder restricts the chest and prevents deep breathing

B — lying flat on the back all day: Lying flat all day does not clear the passages

D — complete rest without moving: Rest without moving lets the secretions collect

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse teaches the patient to take two or three deep breaths and then to cough once, because a series of small coughs tires the patient and moves very little
option_1: the use of a tight abdominal binder
option_2: lying flat on the back all day
option_3: deep breathing and coughing with the wound or the chest supported

question: A 50-year-old woman on the first day after abdominal surgery has a pulse of 118 per minute and a blood pressure of 90 by 60 mm Hg. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. check the dressing and the drain for bleeding, look for internal bleeding and inform the doctor at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A fast pulse with a falling blood pressure on the first day after surgery points to bleeding or fluid loss, so the wound and the drain are checked and the doctor is called at once

🔍 Key Clues: 50-year-old | 118 per minute | 60 mm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — raise her legs only: Raising the legs is not enough on its own

B — give a hot drink: A hot drink is not the treatment of such a change

C — record it as a normal postoperative change: Such a change is not a normal finding

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse counts the pulse and takes the pressure before and after any change of dressing, because a fall in the pressure after the dressing is looked at tells that the bleeding is still going on
option_3: record it as a normal postoperative change
option_4: check the dressing and the drain for bleeding, look for internal bleeding and inform the doctor at once

question: At the bedside of a patient with a tracheostomy the nurse must always keep:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a spare tracheostomy tube of the same size, suction apparatus and an Ambu bag

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A spare tube of the same size, suction and a means of giving breathing support are kept ready for the moment the tube is blocked or comes out

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a weighing scale: A weighing scale is not kept at the bedside for this purpose

B — a feeding cup and a spoon: A feeding cup is not the emergency need

D — a hot water bottle: A hot water bottle is dangerous near a patient with an airway problem

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks the spare tube and the suction every shift, because a tube that has been in the cupboard for months may be of the wrong size when it is needed in a hurry
option_3: a spare tracheostomy tube of the same size, suction apparatus and an Ambu bag

question: The nurse cleans a surgical wound from the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. centre towards the outer edge, using a fresh swab for each stroke

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cleaning from the centre outwards carries the organisms away from the wound, and a fresh swab for each stroke avoids taking them back

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — left side to the right side only: Working only from side to side does not follow the principle of cleanliness

C — lower end to the upper end: The direction up or down is not the rule

D — outer edge towards the centre: Cleaning inwards drags the organisms of the surrounding skin into the wound

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse uses the swab once and discards it, because a swab taken back over an area that has just been cleaned undoes the whole of the work
option_1: centre towards the outer edge, using a fresh swab for each stroke
option_2: left side to the right side only

question: A 40-year-old woman receiving a blood transfusion becomes breathless with a raised jugular pulse and a fall in blood pressure. The nurse should first:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. stop the transfusion, keep the line open with saline and inform the doctor at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Breathlessness with a raised jugular pulse and a falling pressure in a transfusion points to an overload or a reaction, so the transfusion is stopped, the line kept open with saline and the doctor called at once

🔍 Key Clues: 40-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — increase the rate to finish the unit quickly: A faster rate would make the overload worse

B — ask her to breathe into a paper bag: Breathing into a bag is dangerous and has no place here

D — sit her up and continue the transfusion slowly: Continuing the transfusion, even slowly, keeps the cause in place

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the amount transfused and the time of the first sign, because the doctor decides the further treatment from how much blood had gone in before the reaction began
option_1: increase the rate to finish the unit quickly
option_2: ask her to breathe into a paper bag
option_3: stop the transfusion, keep the line open with saline and inform the doctor at once
option_4: sit her up and continue the transfusion slowly

question: The number of antenatal visits advised for a woman with a normal pregnancy in India is at least:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. four

🧠 Clinical Rationale: At least four antenatal visits are advised for a normal pregnancy in the national programme, and more if any problem appears

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — eight: Eight visits may be advised for a high risk pregnancy

C — twelve: Twelve visits is far more than is required for a normal pregnancy

D — two: Two visits are too few to follow the progress of the pregnancy

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes the date of the next visit on the card and explains what will be done on that day, because a mother who knows what to expect keeps the appointment

question: A woman on the second day after delivery complains of after pains while feeding her baby. The nurse should explain that these pains:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. are caused by the uterus contracting and are a normal sign

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The uterus contracts after delivery, and the pains worsen while feeding because the sucking releases a hormone that makes it contract harder

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — mean that an infection is beginning: After pains in the first days are normal and not a sign of infection

C — mean that the uterus is not contracting: The contractions are exactly what is wanted

D — require the baby to be taken off the breast: Feeding helps the uterus to contract and is continued

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse reassures the mother and gives the ordered mild analgesic, because a mother who fears the pain may feed the baby less and the milk supply then falls
option_1: are caused by the uterus contracting and are a normal sign
option_3: mean that the uterus is not contracting
option_4: require the baby to be taken off the breast

question: Immediately after birth the newborn is kept warm best by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. drying him and keeping him skin to skin on the mother with both covered

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Drying the baby and putting him skin to skin on the mother's chest, both of them covered, keeps the temperature steady and encourages breastfeeding

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — placing him under a fan: A fan cools the baby and is dangerous

C — giving him a bath at once: A bath at once lowers the temperature and is not done immediately

D — wrapping him loosely in a wet sheet: A wet sheet draws the heat away from the body

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse covers the baby's head as well, because a newborn loses much of the heat from the head and a cold baby feeds poorly and may become ill
option_1: drying him and keeping him skin to skin on the mother with both covered
option_4: wrapping him loosely in a wet sheet

question: On the partograph the line of cervical dilatation has crossed the alert line. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. inform the doctor at once and prepare for the steps needed to speed up the labour

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Crossing the alert line means the labour is slower than it should be, so the doctor is informed at once and the steps to correct the progress are prepared

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a sedative: A sedative does not correct a slow labour

B — stop recording the dilatation: Recording is continued and becomes more important

D — wait for the next examination: Waiting lets the delay worsen and the baby suffer

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse plots the line at every examination without delay, because the alert line warns in good time only when the plotting is honest and up to date
option_3: inform the doctor at once and prepare for the steps needed to speed up the labour

question: The Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme is built mainly on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a full course of treatment taken under direct supervision, with the sputum checked at fixed intervals

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The programme rests on a full course of treatment taken under supervision without a break, with the sputum examined at fixed points to prove the cure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — treating only the very ill patients: Treating only the severely ill leaves the infectious cases spreading the disease

C — giving the drugs only when the fever is high: Drugs given only with fever are stopped and started, which breeds resistance

D — isolating every patient for a year: Isolation for a year is neither needed nor possible

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps the treatment card and marks every dose, because a patient who has taken most of the course and stopped feels well and believes wrongly that he is cured
option_2: a full course of treatment taken under direct supervision, with the sputum checked at fixed intervals
option_3: giving the drugs only when the fever is high

question: An ASHA brings a woman in the eighth month of pregnancy with swelling of the feet and a blood pressure of 150 by 100 mm Hg. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. refer her to the first referral unit at once and inform the medical officer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A blood pressure this high with swelling in the last weeks of pregnancy needs referral at once so that pre-eclampsia is managed before a fit occurs

🔍 Key Clues: 100 mm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — advise her to reduce the salt and come back after a month: A wait of a month is far too long in this condition

C — ask her to walk home and rest: Walking home is unsafe for a woman who may fit at any moment

D — give her iron and calcium tablets only: Iron and calcium do not treat a high blood pressure

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse writes down the blood pressure, the urine result and the time of referral on the slip that goes with her, because the referral unit acts on the first reading only if it has been measured and recorded
option_1: advise her to reduce the salt and come back after a month
option_2: refer her to the first referral unit at once and inform the medical officer
option_3: ask her to walk home and rest
option_4: give her iron and calcium tablets only

question: The nurse explains that water for drinking in a village is made safe at home most simply by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. boiling it and storing it covered

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Boiling kills the organisms in the water, and storing it covered in a clean vessel keeps it safe afterwards

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — keeping it in the sun: Sunlight alone does not make water safe to drink

C — adding sugar: Sugar feeds the organisms and makes the water worse

D — filtering it through a cloth only: A cloth removes the mud but not the organisms

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse says that water which has been boiled must be poured into the same vessel or it becomes unsafe again, because the commonest fault is to store safe water in a dirty pot

question: The most effective method of teaching a village group about hand washing is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a demonstration in which the group washes its own hands and is then asked to repeat it at home

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Learning that includes doing and repeating leaves the skill behind, and doing it in the group makes it acceptable to the whole village

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — putting up a poster in the health centre only: A poster in the centre is not seen by those who do not come

B — reading out the instructions at a meeting: Reading out instructions is forgotten by the time the meeting ends

D — distributing printed leaflets alone: A leaflet alone reaches only those who can read and do not throw it away

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse asks the group to bring soap or ash and water so that the demonstration is done with what the family actually has at home
option_1: putting up a poster in the health centre only
option_2: reading out the instructions at a meeting
option_3: a demonstration in which the group washes its own hands and is then asked to repeat it at home

question: A baby usually begins to hold the head steady by the age of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. three months

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Head control becomes steady at about three months, and the baby turns the head to follow a person

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — six months: By six months the baby can sit with some support and rolls over

C — one month: At one month the head still falls back

D — nine months: By nine months the baby sits without support and may crawl

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse checks the milestones at every visit to the well baby clinic, because a milestone that is late is the earliest sign that the development needs looking into

question: A 1-year-old child with diarrhoea is alert with moist eyes and there is a slow return of the skin pinch. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. start oral rehydration solution and teach the mother to continue it at home after each loose stool

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The child has some dehydration, which is treated with oral rehydration solution and continued at home after every loose stool

🔍 Key Clues: 1-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give an antibiotic without a doctor's order: An antibiotic is given only when the doctor orders it for a specific reason

B — withhold all fluids for six hours: Withholding fluids lets the dehydration deepen

C — give only plain water and no salts: Plain water does not replace the salts that have been lost

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse shows the mother exactly how much solution to give after each stool and makes her give a dose in the clinic, because a mother who has done it once under the nurse's eyes does it correctly at home
option_1: give an antibiotic without a doctor's order
option_3: give only plain water and no salts
option_4: start oral rehydration solution and teach the mother to continue it at home after each loose stool

question: A newborn has a yellow tinge of the skin on the first day of life. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. inform the doctor at once, since jaundice on the first day is always abnormal

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The usual jaundice of the newborn appears after the first twenty four hours, so a yellow tinge on the first day is abnormal and is reported at once

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — treat it as the usual physiological jaundice and wait: Waiting on the first day could miss a severe haemolytic cause

C — stop the breastfeeding: Feeding is continued, since it helps to remove the pigment

D — put the baby in the sun and give extra water: Sun and extra water do not treat jaundice that begins so early

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse examines the baby in good daylight and presses the skin over the nose to see the colour, because a yellow tinge is easily missed under a yellow ward light
option_1: treat it as the usual physiological jaundice and wait
option_2: inform the doctor at once, since jaundice on the first day is always abnormal
option_4: put the baby in the sun and give extra water

question: The nurse must watch a patient closely during the first minutes after an intravenous injection of penicillin because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a severe allergic reaction may begin within minutes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A severe allergic reaction to penicillin can begin within minutes, and the antidote and the oxygen are kept ready

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the drug is painful: Pain is not the first concern and is not life threatening

B — the drug lowers the blood sugar: Penicillin does not lower the blood sugar

D — the drug must be given slowly: The rate matters but the reason for the watch is the reaction

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse asks about an earlier reaction to penicillin at every admission, because the second reaction is usually far more severe than the first
option_3: a severe allergic reaction may begin within minutes

question: A 30-year-old woman in the first three months of pregnancy is prescribed a drug whose safety in pregnancy is unknown. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. check the prescription with the doctor, explain the reason and ask whether a safer drug is available

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In the first three months the organs are being formed, so a drug of unknown safety is queried with the doctor before it is given

🔍 Key Clues: 30-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — halve the dose and give it: Altering a dose is not the nurse's decision

B — give it as prescribed without a word: A nurse who identifies a risk does not pass it by

C — stop all drugs for the patient: Stopping all drugs may harm the mother and the baby

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse also asks the mother about any drug she has already taken, because the first weeks are exactly the time when many women do not yet know that they are pregnant
option_2: give it as prescribed without a word
option_4: check the prescription with the doctor, explain the reason and ask whether a safer drug is available

question: A patient on digoxin is prescribed a diuretic that removes potassium. The nurse should plan to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. have the serum potassium and the digoxin level checked and watch for the signs of digoxin toxicity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A low potassium makes the heart more sensitive to digoxin, so the levels are checked and the signs of toxicity are watched

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give both drugs together and take no further steps: Taking no steps leaves the patient open to a dangerous reaction

B — double the digoxin dose: A larger dose would worsen the problem

C — stop the diuretic without an order: The nurse does not stop a drug on her own

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse notes the potassium result against the digoxin dose, because the danger lies in the two results taken together and each of them alone may look acceptable
option_1: give both drugs together and take no further steps
option_4: have the serum potassium and the digoxin level checked and watch for the signs of digoxin toxicity

question: The tube that carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. ureter

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The ureter carries the urine formed in the kidney down to the bladder, one on each side

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — urethra: The urethra carries the urine out of the bladder to the outside

B — collecting duct: The collecting duct carries the urine within the kidney itself

D — renal artery: The renal artery brings blood to the kidney

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse watches the urine output and any pain in the loin after a stone has been treated, because a stone that has moved into the ureter causes colic and may obstruct the flow on that side

question: The part of the nervous system that controls the heartbeat, the breathing and the blood pressure without our will is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. autonomic nervous system

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The autonomic nervous system works without our will and controls the heart, the breathing, the blood pressure and the glands

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — somatic nervous system: The somatic system governs the voluntary muscles

B — the spinal cord only: The spinal cord carries and reflexes but is not the whole of this system

C — the cerebrum: The cerebrum governs thought and voluntary movement

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse understands why the pulse and the breathing carry on during sleep and unconsciousness, and why these are the first signs to change when a patient deteriorates

question: A 40-year-old man admitted after a suicide attempt says nothing and turns his face to the wall. The best action of the nurse is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. sit with him quietly, show that she is ready to listen and stay with him

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Silence with the nurse present and unhurried is often what allows the patient to speak, and the presence itself gives protection

🔍 Key Clues: 40-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tell him that his act was wrong: A moral judgement adds to the feeling of worthlessness

B — question him at length about the attempt: A long questioning at this time closes the patient up further

C — leave him alone for the whole shift: Leaving such a patient alone is the most dangerous step

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse says in simple words that she will stay and that he does not have to speak, because a patient who knows he is not being pressed begins to talk sooner
option_1: tell him that his act was wrong
option_2: question him at length about the attempt
option_3: leave him alone for the whole shift
option_4: sit with him quietly, show that she is ready to listen and stay with him

question: A patient admitted for alcohol withdrawal develops tremors, sweating and a pulse of 120 per minute. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. keep him in a calm well lit place, record the pulse and the blood pressure often, give the ordered sedation and fluids, and watch for a fit

🧠 Clinical Rationale: These are the signs of withdrawal, and the patient needs a calm place, close observation, the ordered sedation and fluids, and a watch for fits

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a hot drink and wait: Hot drinks do not help and waiting lets the withdrawal deepen

B — leave him in a dark room alone: A dark room alone increases the fear and the hallucinations

C — restrain him at once: Restraint is used only when nothing else will prevent injury

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the pulse and the blood pressure every few hours, because a rising pulse with a falling pressure is among the earliest warnings that the withdrawal is becoming severe
option_2: leave him in a dark room alone
option_4: keep him in a calm well lit place, record the pulse and the blood pressure often, give the ordered sedation and fluids, and watch for a fit

question: The nurse should not use an autoclave pack that is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. damp or torn and whose date of sterilisation has long passed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A damp or torn pack has lost its sterility, since the wrapper is the barrier, and a pack kept beyond the set period is no longer safe

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — labelled with the date: Labelling with the date is the correct practice

B — warm after the cycle: A pack that is still warm after the cycle is normal and does not spoil its sterility

C — kept in a closed cupboard: A closed cupboard is a proper place of storage

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse opens the pack only at the moment of use and never leaves it open on the trolley, because a wrapper once opened cannot be closed to keep the articles sterile again
option_4: damp or torn and whose date of sterilisation has long passed

question: A wound is hot, red, swollen and painful with a thin discharge in the first two days. The nurse recognises this as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the normal inflammation of healing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Heat, redness, swelling and pain in the first days after a wound are the normal signs of inflammation, which brings the blood and the cells that repair the tissue

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a drug reaction: A drug reaction gives a rash rather than these local signs

C — a malignant change: A malignant change does not appear in the first two days

D — an infection with pus: An infection usually gives thick pus with a fever and appears later

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse records the day on which the discharge changes in volume or colour, because an infection that sets in on top of normal inflammation is recognised by the change and not by the presence of the discharge

question: In a patient with chronic kidney disease the nurse teaches a diet that is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. low in protein, low in salt and low in potassium, with a measured fluid intake

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A failing kidney cannot remove the waste of protein or the potassium, and it holds water, so the protein, the salt, the potassium and the fluids are all controlled

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — rich in protein and potassium: A diet rich in potassium and protein would overload a failing kidney

B — very high in salt to replace the loss: Extra salt raises the blood pressure further

C — made up of raw salads alone: Raw salads alone do not give a balanced diet

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse tells the patient the exact number of glasses of fluid he may take in a day, because advice to take less fluid without a number is followed only until the first hot day
option_2: very high in salt to replace the loss
option_4: low in protein, low in salt and low in potassium, with a measured fluid intake

question: The largest island in the world is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Greenland

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Greenland covers over two million square kilometres and is by far the largest island in the world

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — New Guinea: New Guinea is the second largest island

B — Borneo: Borneo is the third largest island

D — Madagascar: Madagascar is the fourth largest island

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse keeps a small world map in the ward teaching room, because a patient or a child shown where a place is remembers the health talk that went with it

question: The title Deshbandhu was given to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Chittaranjan Das

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Chittaranjan Das was known as Deshbandhu, the friend of the country, for his service and his sacrifice

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Lala Lajpat Rai: Lala Lajpat Rai was known as the Lion of Punjab

B — Madan Mohan Malaviya: Madan Mohan Malaviya was called Mahamana

C — Motilal Nehru: Motilal Nehru was a leader of the Congress and had other titles

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who knows the selfless service of such leaders finds the same spirit in the community health worker who walks to a far village for one child's vaccine

question: The National Human Rights Commission of India was established in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1993

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The National Human Rights Commission was set up in 1993 under an Act of Parliament to protect the rights of the people

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 2000: 2000 is later

C — 2005: 2005 is later still

D — 1985: 1985 is earlier than its setting up

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who knows that a patient's rights have a body behind them is less afraid to speak up when the care given is not what it should be

question: The Duleep Trophy is associated with:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. cricket

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Duleep Trophy is a first class cricket tournament played between zones of India

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tennis: Tennis has the Davis Cup and the Grand Slam events

B — football: Football has the Santosh Trophy and others

C — hockey: Hockey has other trophies

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who lets a long stay patient follow his own game on the radio gives him something to look forward to, and a patient with something to look forward to co-operates better with the treatment

question: Operation Flood, a programme of the Government of India, is associated with the production of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. milk

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Operation Flood was the programme that built the milk co-operative system and raised the production of milk in the country

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — pulses: Pulses were not the subject of this programme

B — fish: Fish production is the Blue Revolution

D — wheat: Wheat production is linked with the Green Revolution

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse adds milk or another protein food to the diet of a pregnant woman when it can be afforded, because the growth of the baby depends on the protein taken by the mother

question: The Rowlatt Act was passed in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 1919

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 allowed the arrest and detention of a person without trial, and it was opposed all over the country

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1929: 1929 is the year of the Lahore session and the call for complete independence

B — 1909: 1909 is the year of the Morley-Minto reforms

C — 1935: 1935 is the year of the Government of India Act

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who has seen how a community responds to a law that is felt to be unjust understands why a health rule must be explained before it is enforced

question: The newspaper Kesari was started by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Bal Gangadhar Tilak

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Bal Gangadhar Tilak started Kesari in Marathi and Maratha in English to carry the message of the national movement to the people

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Gopal Krishna Gokhale: Gopal Krishna Gokhale edited the journal of the Servants of India Society

C — Mahatma Gandhi: Mahatma Gandhi edited Young India and Harijan

D — Dadabhai Naoroji: Dadabhai Naoroji was a leader and an economist

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who writes a health message in the local language for the village wall reaches far more people than one who writes it in English, which is the same lesson these newspapers carried

question: The first recipient of the Bharat Ratna was:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. C Rajagopalachari

🧠 Clinical Rationale: C Rajagopalachari was among the first recipients of the Bharat Ratna in 1954, along with C V Raman and S Radhakrishnan

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Jawaharlal Nehru: Jawaharlal Nehru received it later

C — S Radhakrishnan: S Radhakrishnan was also among the first recipients, but the question asks for the one named here as the first grantee in the usual list

D — B R Ambedkar: B R Ambedkar received it much later

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse who knows the service behind such an award understands that recognition follows work and never precedes it, which is as true of a nurse's career as of anyone else's

question: The gas that makes up most of the air we breathe is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. nitrogen

🧠 Clinical Rationale: About four fifths of the air is nitrogen, and only about one fifth is oxygen

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — argon: Argon is present in a small quantity

B — carbon dioxide: Carbon dioxide is present only in a very small amount

D — oxygen: Oxygen is the gas we need but it is not the largest part of the air

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse knows that a patient on oxygen is breathing oxygen added to this mixture and not pure oxygen, which is why the flow is set carefully on the flow meter

question: The enzyme in the saliva acts mainly on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. starch
